findings.text: Guest CPUID management is exposed through three VCPU operations handling legacy set, extended set and extended query. The legacy variant accepts older entry shape and widens it, while extended variants exchange current entry shape directly. All three enforce an upper bound on entry count and delegate persistence or retrieval to shared per-VCPU state.

Host capability discovery is available as a one time global initialization that builds a per leaf table of supportable guest features from kernel data, host probing and local policy adjustments. Later helpers query or adjust individual feature bits only while this construction window is active.

Per VCPU Hyper-V state creation is offered under one name with two build dependent behaviours. When the feature is enabled it allocates and prepares synthetic interrupt, timer and flush structures on first use and leaves existing state untouched. When disabled it reports success without acting.
Support for automatically restored host MSRs is queryable through a predicate that reports membership in a maintained list, backed by a linear scan returning position or absence.

A bounded collection used during enumeration holds a pointer to storage plus capacity and current fill count. Allocation of next slot fails gracefully once full, preventing overflow and letting callers signal excess to userspace.

Hyper-V context attached to a VCPU groups synthetic interrupt state, several timers with pending indication, an index mirroring VCPU order, and multiple flush queues each paired with its own synchronization primitive. Publication uses ordering that makes fully prepared state visible to concurrent readers.
Each synthetic timer owns a preformed expiry notice whose header carries a fixed type and a payload length, while payload carries timer identity with cleared timing fields awaiting later update.

Installation of new guest CPUID data never discards prior state until validation succeeds. Former entries and capability snapshots are retained during staging, restored unchanged on error, and only replaced plus old storage released after acceptance.

Contexts where full model change is unsafe accept only data equal to current configuration, avoiding disruption to address width handling, large page support and nested execution. Unrestricted contexts proceed to consistency checks and post update finalization including hypervisor specific refresh.

Each leaf value starts from declared desirable features, is narrowed by kernel support, widened by explicitly allowed passthrough, narrowed again by host measurement plus locally synthesized items, then widened by emulated items. Misuse where a feature is declared under wrong leaf is caught at build time.

Some declarations record awareness without granting guest visibility. Vendor gated and runtime managed names are validated for leaf placement but do not contribute to advertised support, while scattered and bitness gated variants contribute only when host or build conditions hold. One aliasing helper mirrors a subset from another leaf under strict placement checks.

Host leaf collection synthesizes hypervisor range locally, guards extended range with a cached maximum to avoid out of range queries, otherwise executes hardware query and marks architecturally indexed functions accordingly.

Each flush queue has a dedicated write synchronization object initialized alongside queue storage. The Hyper-V context pointer itself is published with release ordering so concurrent observers outside mutual exclusion see coherent state, paired with acquire load on read path.

Guest CPUID evolves through stable, staged and resolved conditions. Stale dynamic information is refreshed before staging, staged content is validated, then outcome is either committed with cleanup of superseded storage or abandoned with restoration of prior snapshot.

Global capability construction moves from cleared through configuring to sealed. During configuring each leaf is assembled and policy adjustments apply based on paging mode, host abilities and anomaly reports. Mutation helpers warn if invoked outside configuring.

Contracts for userspace control include count limits on all paths, kernel duplication of user arrays with allocation failure reporting on set paths, ownership transfer to shared installer, and on query a destination capacity requirement with prior refresh of stale dynamic state followed by copy out and actual count reporting.

Altering core model after first run or while nested guest is active risks reuse of stale address translation metadata and misconfigured nested state. Implementation mitigates by allowing only identical data in those contexts, preserving legacy callers that repeat setup during hotplug.

Excessive entry counts, failed user duplication, failed kernel allocation and full enumeration buffers are all reported without mutating committed state. Query with undersized destination and host enumeration overflow similarly fail cleanly, leaving prior configuration intact.

Misreporting timestamp counter identifier features when auxiliary MSR probing failed would likely crash guests. Startup sanity logic hides both related features if either appears supported without corresponding MSR support.
The limit known as KVM_MAX_CPUID_ENTRIES governs how many entries userspace may supply or retrieve in one call, with excess rejected and no state change.

Synthetic interrupt state starts at version HV_SYNIC_VERSION_1 with each channel initially masked via HV_SYNIC_SINT_MASKED and unmapped. Timer expiry notices use type HVMSG_TIMER_EXPIRED. Underlying timers run on CLOCK_MONOTONIC in absolute mode HRTIMER_MODE_ABS.
Host probing accepts bases 0x0 and 0x80000000 and 0xc0000000 and rejects others. Indexed functions carry KVM_CPUID_FLAG_SIGNIFCANT_INDEX.
Unknown vendor families and leaves beyond hardware maximum yield absence without hardware access. Otherwise result reflects counted hardware state for requested register.
Existing context causes immediate success with no change. Fresh context is zeroed, linked to owner, indexed by VCPU order, with cleared pending indication, fully prepared before becoming visible.
Legacy entry shape is widened to extended shape by copying architectural registers and function identifier while clearing subleaf selector, option flags and reserved words.
Emulated leaf expansion appends synthesized entries into remaining capacity, failing with excess indication when no room remains.
